type.description: The stable category URI. Switch on this, never on `title`.

bearerAuth.description: A `tm_` API key, minted on a project's API keys page. It reads its organization and that project, within the scopes it was minted with: an upload needs `ingest`, as an export does, and every other lane here `read`.

info.description: The API a `tm_` token opens. Every response that is not a success is an RFC 9457 problem document, and a client switches on its `type` rather than on its prose.
info.title: Telmoni API

put.description: An image, audio or a file a span's message carried, sent once by the SHA-256 of its bytes, which its message then names as `telmoni:` and the hash. Kept, sealed, for a project that keeps content, and nothing for one that does not; sent again, it changes nothing.

parameters.description: The SHA-256 of the body, in lowercase hex.
parameters.name: sha256

requestBody.description: The bytes, their media type as `Content-Type`.

204.description: Kept, kept already, or nothing kept for a project that keeps no content or an organization that holds the content its plan does.

400.description: A hash that is not the body's.

401.description: No live `tm_` API key was presented. A revoked, expired or unknown key answers the same way.

429.description: Too many requests. The server meters by source address and by key before the request reaches a lane, and says when to come back in `Retry-After`.

503.description: The lane is switched off, or something it needs did not answer. A switched-off lane says when to try again in `Retry-After`.

put.summary: Keep a file a message carried

get.description: Everyone on the project the key was minted on, the owner first, with the role each holds. The same list the console's project roster shows, so a key reads no more than the project admin who minted it could; the organization's roster is the console's alone.

200.description: The members: the owner, then the project's seats.

get.description: The organization the key belongs to — its id, its slug, its name and its owner's address and name. The slug is what the console's URLs name it by: set from the name it was created under, when that reads as one, and moved only when the URL is changed in Settings; the id never moves. A key is minted on one project of one organization, so this answers for the caller's organization and for no other.
